about: The build's task tree, derived from blueprint by packages/plan/src/tasks.ts (docs/design/swarm.md, section 5). Do not edit: change the blueprint or the script, then regenerate. It holds no counts over the blueprint, so lanes that change different tasks never conflict here.

tasks.title: Capxul rebuilt
tasks.goal: Capxul runs on the new stack and does everything the built blueprint's operations promise (the old 215 less what the cut classified, plus the plugs and the door): every eval passes at the head of integration/build on a devnet, the system evals and the size budget hold, and staging's live evals hold for a week.

tasks.title: Foundation: the book complete and fit for purpose
tasks.goal: The cut; the plugs, sites and the door written into the book in full; where each operation stands is recorded; and the book fit to build from.

exit.claim: Every part of the system is a record, the machine, the worlds, the site service and a production environment included.
The book builds with no problems and every open gap is closed or has a recorded reason.
Every operation has an example and names its telemetry.
Where code exists a check proves the book matches it.
Everything the spikes found is a record or a decision.
The plan page is generated and current.
Aaron reads the portal and accepts it.

A shared world runs on the sites machine, not a laptop, created by one command, with a thin line through every part of the stack proven by tests that run there: the real contracts on its chain, the service, a company's site, the door, a payment held and signed by key, the record, the clock, and a s…

tasks.title: Real chain under the test sites
tasks.goal: The v4 contracts in this repository with their tests; a seeded chain state so nothing needs the network; a key-based agent signer; the skeleton's stand-in chain replaced.

exit.claim: The skeleton's checks pass against the real contracts: a hat granted through Hats, a budget set, a payment sent through Payments under that hat and budget with the document's hash.

tasks.title: The door, the recorder and the clock
tasks.goal: The CLI reaches Frappe's documents, actions and reports as the calling person; every command is recorded; a world's time is moved from the CLI and the site and chain follow it. Built in parallel with m2.

exit.claim: An agent takes a lead to a paid invoice, onboards a staff member and runs a month end through the CLI only, on a clock it moved, and the whole run can be read back from the record.

tasks.title: The cloud: worlds on a machine, not a laptop
tasks.goal: How a bench of company sites, the service, a chain and the record run on the existing cloud, written down and then stood up.

exit.claim: A world running in the cloud that a person can open in a browser while agents drive it.

tasks.title: The compatibility climb
tasks.goal: The Core operations built to the book, group by group, with the old code as the reference for behaviour.

exit.claim: The score: kept operations passing their evals on the real stack, group by group. No number is promised before milestone 2 is done.

tasks.title: Company life: months on the real stack
tasks.goal: A multi-month run on the real stack, from the old scenario histories.

exit.claim: The books agree with the chain at every month end, over a multi-month run from the old scenario histories.

tasks.title: auth list: List signed-in people
tasks.goal: `capxul auth list` does what operation auth.list promises: its 1 acceptance claims and 2 refusals hold, its --json shape, events, spans and budget pass on a devnet at the head of integration/build, and its reference page agrees with it. Lists the people signed in on this machine and marks the current one. Each row says whether the person is a human or an AI that signs with its own key. Use it to see who you can switch to.

tasks.title: auth logout: Sign out
tasks.goal: `capxul auth logout` does what operation auth.logout promises: its 1 acceptance claims and 2 refusals hold, its --json shape, events, spans and budget pass on a devnet at the head of integration/build, and its reference page agrees with it. Signs a person out on this device. Without `--email` it signs out the current person. It removes the session here first and then asks the backend to revoke it.

tasks.title: auth switch: Switch person
tasks.goal: `capxul auth switch` does what operation auth.switch promises: its 1 acceptance claims and 2 refusals hold, its --json shape, events, spans and budget pass on a devnet at the head of integration/build, and its reference page agrees with it. Makes another person who is already signed in on this machine the current one. At a terminal you can leave out the email and pick from a list, which also offers to sign in someone else. The CLI checks the session with the backend before it switches.

tasks.title: config telemetry off: Turn telemetry off
tasks.goal: `capxul config telemetry off` does what operation config.telemetry.off promises: its 3 acceptance claims and 2 refusals hold, its --json shape, events, spans and budget pass on a devnet at the head of integration/build, and its reference page agrees with it. tasks.title: config telemetry on: Turn telemetry on

tasks.title: config telemetry status: Telemetry status

Shows whether this CLI collects usage and diagnostics. It also says when this build has no place to send them, or when an environment variable forces collection off.

tasks.title: schema: Read the command schema
tasks.goal: `capxul schema` does what operation schema promises: its 4 acceptance claims and 1 refusals hold, its --json shape, events, spans and budget pass on a devnet at the head of integration/build, and its reference page agrees with it. Prints the CLI's own description as JSON. With no words it lists every command, whether it moves money, the global flags and the exit codes. With a command, such as `capxul schema payment send`, it gives that command's arguments, flags, output and error codes. Agents use it to look up a command instead of guessing flags.

tasks.title: use env: Choose an environment
tasks.goal: `capxul use env` does what operation use.env promises: its 1 acceptance claims and 2 refusals hold, its --json shape, events, spans and budget pass on a devnet at the head of integration/build, and its reference page agrees with it. Saves the environment later commands use: devnet, staging, beta or production. The CLI has no built-in default, so you choose one before the first command that needs the network.

tasks.title: use personal: Act as yourself
tasks.goal: `capxul use personal` does what operation use.personal promises: its 1 acceptance claims and 2 refusals hold, its --json shape, events, spans and budget pass on a devnet at the head of integration/build, and its reference page agrees with it. Makes later commands act for you yourself instead of an Organization. Use it after `capxul use org` to go back to your own account.

tasks.title: whoami: Who am I
tasks.goal: `capxul whoami` does what operation whoami promises: its 1 acceptance claims and 1 refusals hold, its --json shape, events, spans and budget pass on a devnet at the head of integration/build, and its reference page agrees with it. Shows who you are, who you act as, the Safe and the environment. It reads only files on this machine, so it answers fast and makes no network call. With `--json` it also says where each value came from.

tasks.title: account retry: Finish account setup
tasks.goal: `capxul account retry` does what operation account.retry promises: its 1 acceptance claims and 3 refusals hold, its --json shape, events, spans and budget pass on a devnet at the head of integration/build, and its reference page agrees with it. Tells you where to finish setting up your account, or confirms it is ready. If setup is not done, it returns the web app link to finish it in your browser. Run it again after you finish to check.

tasks.title: auth login: Sign in
tasks.goal: `capxul auth login` does what operation auth.login promises: its 2 acceptance claims and 3 refusals hold, its --json shape, events, spans and budget pass on a devnet at the head of integration/build, and its reference page agrees with it. Signs you in with your email and a six-digit code sent to it. At a terminal it sends the code, asks for it and finishes in one go. In a script, an agent or a `--json` run without `--otp-stdin`, it only sends the code and tells you to finish with `capxul auth verify <code>`. With `--own-key` it sets up an AI's own account, which signs with its own key.

tasks.title: auth verify: Finish signing in
tasks.goal: `capxul auth verify` does what operation auth.verify promises: its 2 acceptance claims and 1 refusals hold, its --json shape, events, spans and budget pass on a devnet at the head of integration/build, and its reference page agrees with it. Finishes a sign-in that `capxul auth login` started without a terminal. You give it the six-digit code from the email, as an argument or on standard input with `--otp-stdin`. Scripts and agents use it as the second of two sign-in commands.

Shows where your account's setup stands: loading, setting up (with the step), ready, or failed (with the step and error code). It reads the state and never starts or resumes setup.

tasks.title: dev fund: Fund with test money

Adds test money to your own Safe from the deployment's faucet. With `--org <handle>` it funds that Organization's Safe instead. Use it to have money to try payments with.

Declines an invitation sent to you. The offer ends, and anything it had set up on the chain is cleaned up. Only you can decline your own offer.

tasks.title: invite list: List your invitations
tasks.goal: `capxul invite list` does what operation invite.list promises: its 3 acceptance claims and 4 refusals hold, its --json shape, events, spans and budget pass on a devnet at the head of integration/build, and its reference page agrees with it. Lists the invitations sent to you, from any Organization. Each one shows its Organization, phase, expiry and offered grants. Use it to find the invitation ID for `invite accept`. With `--json`, each invitation also carries its offer digest.

tasks.title: org create: Create an Organization
tasks.goal: `capxul org create` does what operation org.create promises: its 7 acceptance claims and 5 refusals hold, its --json shape, events, spans and budget pass on a devnet at the head of integration/build, and its reference page agrees with it. Creates one Organization from a name, a `--handle` and a two-letter `--country`, then follows its setup until it is ready. You sign the founder authorization in your browser. If this machine already recorded a create for the same handle, the command picks up that Organization instead of making a second one.

Cancels an invitation the Organization sent that has not been accepted. Any rights the offer had set up on the chain are then cleaned up. Use it when you invited the wrong person or offered the wrong grants.

The run waits `open`, its clock frozen, until `run start`. Its id (`r` and five digits) is its world's id and its address is `core-<id>.worlds.capxul.com`.

tasks.goal: `capxul run export` does what operation run.export promises: its 2 acceptance claims and 4 refusals hold, its --json shape, events, spans and budget pass on a devnet at the head of integration/build, and its reference page agrees with it. Writes the run's dataset to a folder: `manifest.json` (the run's manifest), `entries.jsonl` (the record, lineage first, one entry a line, with a pseudonym in place of every participant and personal data redacted), `scores.jsonl` (the scenario's measures after each step or day: the rewards), `checks.json` and `ledgers/` (each company's month-end books and chain balances). The schema version is `dataset/1`. A dataset is for training only if every human seat consented to `train` (agent-only runs always); otherwise it is marked evaluation-only.

tasks.title: run seat assign: Put a person or an agent in a seat
tasks.goal: `capxul run seat assign` does what operation run.seat.assign promises: its 2 acceptance claims and 6 refusals hold, its --json shape, events, spans and budget pass on a devnet at the head of integration/build, and its reference page agrees with it. Assigns a seat: `run seat assign r00042 bc-director --agent ledger-agent@1 --key 0x…` or, for a person, `--key 0x…` alone. It makes the invitation bound to that key and, if the key has joined, gives it the seat at once. A person's key and account in the world are the same as an agent's. A seat for a person is specified now and opened after Capxul Core's sign-in exists (aaron.sign-in-is-core): until then a human seat is refused CAPABILITY_UNAVAILABLE and every seat is an agent's.

tasks.title: run seat drop: A participant drops out: apply the run's drop-out policy
tasks.goal: `capxul run seat drop` does what operation run.seat.drop promises: its 1 acceptance claims and 4 refusals hold, its --json shape, events, spans and budget pass on a devnet at the head of integration/build, and its reference page agrees with it. Marks a seat's holder gone (the organiser says so, or the seat's key stopped answering for longer than the scenario allows) and applies the scenario's policy: `agent`: the scenario's agent policy takes the seat, a `handover` entry in the record says from whom to whom and at what world time, and the run goes on; `pause`: the run's world is paused until the seat is filled. The dropped holder's earlier entries stay.

tasks.title: run show: Show one run and how it is going
tasks.goal: `capxul run show` does what operation run.show promises: its 1 acceptance claims and 3 refusals hold, its --json shape, events, spans and budget pass on a devnet at the head of integration/build, and its reference page agrees with it. One run: its state and scenario, who plays each seat (person or agent, and the agent's model), the world's now, the record's head and the addresses of the service and of each company's site.

tasks.title: run start: Start a run's clock plan
tasks.goal: `capxul run start` does what operation run.start promises: its 1 acceptance claims and 4 refusals hold, its --json shape, events, spans and budget pass on a devnet at the head of integration/build, and its reference page agrees with it. Starts the scenario's clock plan: a stepped clock is unfrozen to its first step, a real or fast clock begins running at its rate. Seats that are still open are filled by the scenario's agent policy if the run was made with `--fill-open agent`, otherwise the run refuses to start.

tasks.title: scenario save: Publish a scenario version
tasks.goal: `capxul scenario save` does what operation scenario.save promises: its 1 acceptance claims and 3 refusals hold, its --json shape, events, spans and budget pass on a devnet at the head of integration/build, and its reference page agrees with it. Publishes a scenario version from a manifest file (`--manifest`): the template snapshot, the companies, the seats and which are filled by people and which by agents, the script of outside events, the clock plan, what is scored (the book's evals, plus measures stated as deltas) and when the run ends. A version never changes: a change is `version + 1`, so a run names exactly what it ran. The manifest is checked as `scenario check` checks it.

tasks.title: world clock freeze: Freeze the world's clock
tasks.goal: `capxul world clock freeze` does what operation world.clock.freeze promises: its 1 acceptance claims and 3 refusals hold, its --json shape, events, spans and budget pass on a devnet at the head of integration/build, and its reference page agrees with it. Stops the clock at the world's now; the world then moves only by warp or step.

tasks.title: world clock resume: Resume the world's clock
tasks.goal: `capxul world clock resume` does what operation world.clock.resume promises: its 1 acceptance claims and 3 refusals hold, its --json shape, events, spans and budget pass on a devnet at the head of integration/build, and its reference page agrees with it. Starts a frozen clock again at the rate it had.

tasks.title: world clock set: Run the world's clock at a rate
tasks.goal: `capxul world clock set` does what operation world.clock.set promises: its 1 acceptance claims and 4 refusals hold, its --json shape, events, spans and budget pass on a devnet at the head of integration/build, and its reference page agrees with it. Sets the clock's rate, a whole number 1 to 60 world seconds per real second, preserving frozen or running mode. The chain, the service and every company's site follow.

tasks.title: world clock warp: Move the world's clock forward
tasks.goal: `capxul world clock warp` does what operation world.clock.warp promises: its 1 acceptance claims and 4 refusals hold, its --json shape, events, spans and budget pass on a devnet at the head of integration/build, and its reference page agrees with it. Moves the clock forward by a duration or to a date, stopping at every due instant, running due jobs and moving every follower, the sites included. Not backwards.

tasks.title: world create: Make a whole world
tasks.goal: `capxul world create` does what operation world.create promises: its 5 acceptance claims and 4 refusals hold, its --json shape, events, spans and budget pass on a devnet at the head of integration/build, and its reference page agrees with it. Makes a world: a chain with the contracts, a service, a clock and a record, from a template or empty. `--profile core|full` (default `core`), `--kind local|simulated|staging|production` (default `simulated` on the hosted service, `local` on a laptop), `--clock frozen|running` and `--rate <1 to 60>`. A hosted world answers at `core-<world>.<base>` and its companies at `<company>-<world>.<base>`. `--start-at <date>` sets initial time before anything runs, even before host time; it cannot reset an existing world. Companies are made after with `org create --world`. As easy as making a company.

tasks.title: world grant revoke: Revoke a key's grant in a world
tasks.goal: `capxul world grant revoke` does what operation world.grant.revoke promises: its 2 acceptance claims and 4 refusals hold, its --json shape, events, spans and budget pass on a devnet at the head of integration/build, and its reference page agrees with it. Ends a key's grant at the gateway at once: its next call, and its next page on any company's site address, is refused. In a `full` world its site roles follow (roles follow hats). The seat becomes open (and the run's drop-out policy applies). The key's own record entries stay: the record is never edited. A grant outlives snapshots on purpose: a restore never re-admits it (devnet.shared-world).

tasks.title: world invite create: Make a join link for a world
tasks.goal: `capxul world invite create` does what operation world.invite.create promises: its 2 acceptance claims and 5 refusals hold, its --json shape, events, spans and budget pass on a devnet at the head of integration/build, and its reference page agrees with it. The organiser's one command for a person or agent who already has a key: `world invite create r00042 --role player --seat bc-finance --key 0xabc…` makes a link bound to that key. Without `--key` the link is open and works for its first `--uses` holders of any key. The link is `capxul://join/<world>/<code>`; the code is shown once and stored as a hash. It expires (default 24 hours) and never outlives its run. `--role` is organiser, player or viewer.

tasks.title: world join: Join a world with your key
tasks.goal: `capxul world join` does what operation world.join promises: its 3 acceptance claims and 3 refusals hold, its --json shape, events, spans and budget pass on a devnet at the head of integration/build, and its reference page agrees with it. The participant's one command: `world join <link> --consent run|train`. The CLI signs with the caller's key (`--new-key` makes a test key first for a person who has none: it is held in the CLI's home, holds test money only and is shown once as a recovery phrase). The service checks the invitation, writes the grant, creates the key's account in this world and its Safe at the address that follows from the key and the world, records the consent (the version and the hash of its text) and a `join` entry, grants the seat's hats in its company, and makes this world the current one. Nothing is carried over from any other world. An agent's join is built first. A person's join to play through the screens is specified and waits on Capxul Core's sign-in and sign…

tasks.title: world park: Park a world: storage only
tasks.goal: `capxul world park` does what operation world.park promises: its 1 acceptance claims and 4 refusals hold, its --json shape, events, spans and budget pass on a devnet at the head of integration/build, and its reference page agrees with it. Saves a world and takes it down to storage: the chain's state file, the service's database, the record and, in a `full` world, each company's site as a backup, then drops the sites from the bench. A parked world costs disk only. It is restored on demand: `world resume`, or the first call to its address (the gateway wakes it). Waking a `core` world is seconds (estimate); a `full` world is about 33 seconds per company (measured, the spike's site restore). Idle hosted worlds are parked by the park-idle process.

tasks.title: world pause: Pause a world
tasks.goal: `capxul world pause` does what operation world.pause promises: its 1 acceptance claims and 4 refusals hold, its --json shape, events, spans and budget pass on a devnet at the head of integration/build, and its reference page agrees with it. Stops a world's chain, service and clock where they are and keeps everything in memory-free form on disk: nothing moves and nothing is lost. A run's world paused pauses the run. A paused world still costs its disk and, in a `full` world, its sites' database share, and no memory. The nightly backup also pauses a world for seconds to copy it consistently.

tasks.title: world resume: Resume a paused or parked world
tasks.goal: `capxul world resume` does what operation world.resume promises: its 2 acceptance claims and 5 refusals hold, its --json shape, events, spans and budget pass on a devnet at the head of integration/build, and its reference page agrees with it. Brings a paused world back where it stopped, or restores a parked one from storage. The clock continues from the world's now at the rate it had (a frozen clock stays frozen). A call to a parked world's address does this by itself.

tasks.title: world show: Show one world
tasks.goal: `capxul world show` does what operation world.show promises: its 1 acceptance claims and 2 refusals hold, its --json shape, events, spans and budget pass on a devnet at the head of integration/build, and its reference page agrees with it. A world's companies and their addresses, clock and rate, parent world and snapshot, and the head of its record.

tasks.title: world snapshot restore: Restore a snapshot, in place or into a separate world
tasks.goal: `capxul world snapshot restore` does what operation world.snapshot.restore promises: its 2 acceptance claims and 5 refusals hold, its --json shape, events, spans and budget pass on a devnet at the head of integration/build, and its reference page agrees with it. In place (a new epoch, the abandoned branch kept in the record) or, with `--as <new world>`, into a separate world with the same chain id on a new chain instance, every address renamed, and a `born` entry naming the parent world, snapshot and sequence.

tasks.title: world snapshot save: Save a snapshot of a whole world
tasks.goal: `capxul world snapshot save` does what operation world.snapshot.save promises: its 1 acceptance claims and 4 refusals hold, its --json shape, events, spans and budget pass on a devnet at the head of integration/build, and its reference page agrees with it. Saves the world's chain, service state, every company's site, the clock and the place in the record under a name. `--template` marks it as one new worlds can be made from.

tasks.title: world use: Connect to a world and make it the current one
tasks.goal: `capxul world use` does what operation world.use promises: its 2 acceptance claims and 3 refusals hold, its --json shape, events, spans and budget pass on a devnet at the head of integration/build, and its reference page agrees with it. One CLI, many worlds. `world use <world>` signs a challenge with the caller's key, checks the grant, and stores a connection in the CLI's home: the world's address, the caller's key (a reference, never the key itself) and the grant's role. Every later command goes to that world's service. A flag `--world <name>` or the variable `CAPXUL_WORLD` overrides it for one command. A local devnet is a world whose address is on the laptop (`--address http://127.0.0.1:<port>`).

tasks.title: cohort close: Close a cohort
tasks.goal: `capxul cohort close` does what operation cohort.close promises: its 1 acceptance claims and 4 refusals hold, its --json shape, events, spans and budget pass on a devnet at the head of integration/build, and its reference page agrees with it. Closes every run of the cohort that has not ended (with the reason `cohort closed`), cancels runs not yet opened and marks the cohort closed. Each closed run still has to be checked and exported (`run check`, `run export`, `run accept`).

tasks.title: cohort list: List cohorts
tasks.goal: `capxul cohort list` does what operation cohort.list promises: its 1 acceptance claims and 2 refusals hold, its --json shape, events, spans and budget pass on a devnet at the head of integration/build, and its reference page agrees with it. Cohorts with their scenario, state and how many runs are open, live or done.

tasks.title: dev approve: Approve as someone
tasks.goal: `capxul dev approve` does what operation dev.approve promises: its 0 acceptance claims and 2 refusals hold, its --json shape, events, spans and budget pass on a devnet at the head of integration/build, and its reference page agrees with it. Signs an open approval as another person, with that person's dev signer, as the approval page would. Use it to play every Director or payer in a story from one terminal.

tasks.title: dev gates set: Set a feature gate
tasks.goal: `capxul dev gates set` does what operation dev.gates.set promises: its 0 acceptance claims and 4 refusals hold, its --json shape, events, spans and budget pass on a devnet at the head of integration/build, and its reference page agrees with it. Turns a feature gate on or off for the Organization you name with `--org`. On a devnet, gates come from the devnet's own table.

tasks.title: dev jobs run: Run backend jobs
tasks.goal: `capxul dev jobs run` does what operation dev.jobs.run promises: its 0 acceptance claims and 2 refusals hold, its --json shape, events, spans and budget pass on a devnet at the head of integration/build, and its reference page agrees with it. Runs each backend job once, now, and reports which succeeded. Use it when you want work that runs on a schedule to happen without moving the clocks.

tasks.title: dev mail fail: Fail the next mail
tasks.goal: `capxul dev mail fail` does what operation dev.mail.fail promises: its 3 acceptance claims and 3 refusals hold, its --json shape, events, spans and budget pass on a devnet at the head of integration/build, and its reference page agrees with it. Makes the next writes to the mail sink fail as a provider refusal, so you can see a notice retry. `--to` limits the fault to one address. `--list` shows the faults still armed and `--clear` disarms them all.

tasks.title: dev mail list: Read sent mail
tasks.goal: `capxul dev mail list` does what operation dev.mail.list promises: its 0 acceptance claims and 1 refusals hold, its --json shape, events, spans and budget pass on a devnet at the head of integration/build, and its reference page agrees with it. Shows the mail Capxul sent on the devnet, newest first. Nothing leaves the machine: the devnet keeps it in a mail sink. Use `--to` to see one person's mail, such as an invite or a sign-in code.

tasks.title: dev mail notices: Check notices
tasks.goal: `capxul dev mail notices` does what operation dev.mail.notices promises: its 1 acceptance claims and 1 refusals hold, its --json shape, events, spans and budget pass on a devnet at the head of integration/build, and its reference page agrees with it. Shows each notice's delivery record: sent, retrying or failed, how many attempts, and the last error. The most recently changed come first. Filter by `--to` or `--template`.

tasks.title: dev prices set: Set a USD rate
tasks.goal: `capxul dev prices set` does what operation dev.prices.set promises: its 0 acceptance claims and 4 refusals hold, its --json shape, events, spans and budget pass on a devnet at the head of integration/build, and its reference page agrees with it. Scripts the USD rate of a pair on the devnet, such as `EURC/USD 1.085`. The books use it for money facts written after you set it. Without `--from` it becomes the pair's base rate.

tasks.title: env close: Close an environment
tasks.goal: `capxul env close` does what operation env.close promises: its 1 acceptance claims and 2 refusals hold, its --json shape, events, spans and budget pass on a devnet at the head of integration/build, and its reference page agrees with it. Ends an environment: the run is closed, and its world is destroyed (`--keep` parks it and keeps the dataset). Training loops close thousands; a `core` world frees its memory at once.

tasks.title: env state: Read an environment's state without stepping
tasks.goal: `capxul env state` does what operation env.state promises: its 1 acceptance claims and 2 refusals hold, its --json shape, events, spans and budget pass on a devnet at the head of integration/build, and its reference page agrees with it. The current observation, the measures' current values, the step number and whether the environment is done. No clock moves and no entry is written beyond the read.

Every entry as lines of JSON with the lineage first. The record is training data and a product of the system.

One entry with its redacted arguments, what it returned and changed, its pointers and its cause. No key, token, secret or password is ever in one.

Parks (`--park`, the default: the world can be restored to look at again) or destroys (`--destroy`) the run's world once its dataset is accepted or rejected. The record, the dataset and the run row stay.

tasks.title: run list: List runs

Runs with their state, scenario, cohort and how many seats are filled. `--cohort`, `--state` and `--scenario` filter.

tasks.title: run redact: Withdraw a participant's data from a run
tasks.goal: `capxul run redact` does what operation run.redact promises: its 1 acceptance claims and 4 refusals hold, its --json shape, events, spans and budget pass on a devnet at the head of integration/build, and its reference page agrees with it. A participant withdraws consent: `run redact r00042 --participant p_9c41`. The member row is marked withdrawn, the participant's free text (what they typed in comments, names and notes) is removed from every export, the export is rewritten and marked, and the dataset's training flag becomes false if the withdrawn seat was human. The record itself is never edited: its entries keep the pseudonym and the commands, which hold no personal data once redacted.

tasks.title: scenario check: Check a scenario before publishing it
